import json, shutil, subprocess as s, sys, tempfile, pathlib as P
def plan(N):
    t = P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); c = t / "clone"; c.mkdir()
    shutil.copytree("_tools", c / "_tools", ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "test_*"))
    shutil.copy("backlog.json", c / "backlog.json")
    (c / "kb/_self/backlog").mkdir(parents=True); (c / "kb/_self/backlog/.keep").write_text("")
    def g(*a): return s.run(["git", *a], cwd=c, check=True, capture_output=True)
    g("init", "-q", "-b", "main"); g("config", "user.email", "a@b.c"); g("config", "user.name", "t"); g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
    for i in range(N):
        iid = "ST-p%07d" % i
        (c / "kb/_self/backlog" / (iid + ".json")).write_text('{"id": "%s", "kind": "story", "title": "x", "status": "done"}' % iid)
        g("worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "work/" + iid, ".claude/worktrees/agent-" + iid, "HEAD")
        s.run([sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "own", str(c / ".claude/worktrees" / ("agent-" + iid)), "--class", "worktree", "--item", iid], cwd=c, capture_output=True, check=True)
    p = s.run([sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "tidy", "--older-than", "0", "--json"], cwd=c, capture_output=True, text=True)
    rows = [r for r in json.loads(p.stdout) if r["class"] == "worktree" and "agent-ST-p" in r["path"]]
    return p.returncode, rows
code, rows = plan(5)
few = code == 0 and len(rows) == 5 and all(r["verdict"] == "remove" for r in rows)
code, rows = plan(60)
rm = [r for r in rows if r["verdict"] == "remove"]
rest = [r for r in rows if r["verdict"] != "remove"]
many = code == 0 and 0 < len(rm) <= 25 and len(rm) + len(rest) == 60 and all("status" in r["reason"] for r in rest)
print("5 removable all listed:", few, "; 60 removable:", len(rm), "remove,", len(rest), "kept with a status reason:", many)
sys.exit(0 if few and many else 1)

notes: Found by the SP-vmtfnkim review on 2026-10-26 (BG-xgpnkgth, whose gate g1 answer keeps one git status for each worktree every other check leaves removable): the item's check plants 30 leftovers that are not removable (their items are open), so it counts 13 processes; with 60 leftovers whose items are done and which are clean, merged and idle, tidy --older-than 0 starts 73 git processes, one status each. The repro plants that. No verdict changes and no data is at risk; the process count grows with the removable leftovers, which the goal's fixed number says it should not. A fix needs a way to read the dirtiness of many worktrees in a fixed number of processes, or a bounded goal. Planner's choice (no way reads many worktrees' dirtiness in one git process): a cap of 25 status reads a plan keeps the process count fixed and converges, since --apply removes up to 25 and the next run reads the rest.
